{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABawqoQA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhEWuMU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 54, "title": "Optimize browser CI for CPU-backed SwiftShader without weakening GPU coverage", "body": "## Problem

The browser CI runs Chromium/WebGL through **SwiftShader on CPU-only GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runners** (`playwright.config.ts` explicitly uses `--use-angle=swiftshader` and `--enable-unsafe-swiftshader`, with `workers: 1`). Some browser suites repeatedly compile and execute GPU shader paths across broad Cartesian products of inputs that are also independently checkable by cheap Node/CPU tests.

The question is not whether GPU-path testing is valuable—it is—but **whether each repeated GL draw/readback on a CPU-backed renderer adds distinct coverage worth its CI cost**.

Issue #52 / PR #53 already replaced many redundant screenshot and SDEF/QDEF serialization combinations, while retaining independent conformance. Do not revert or duplicate that work. As of successful PR CI [#69](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/40697950655), the complete 73-test suite on one worker took **35.75 minutes**; the latest successful [#70](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/40706428394) spent **34m21s** in `npm run test:browser`. Previous [#66](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/40159817349) needed **77m28s**, so there has already been meaningful improvement.

Per-file durations recorded from #69's `browser-summary.json`:

| Suite | Time |
| --- | ---: |
| `solver.spec.ts` | 8.71 min (25 tests) |
| `vmd.spec.ts` | 5.21 min (6 tests) |
| `qdef.spec.ts` | 3.41 min (4 tests) |
| `bone-morph.spec.ts` | 2.99 min (4 tests) |
| `uka.spec.ts` | 2.50 min (2 tests) |
| `sdef.spec.ts` | 2.45 min (4 tests) |
| `group.spec.ts` | 2.43 min (5 tests) |
| `physics.spec.ts` | 2.38 min (4 tests) |

`tests/solver-gpu.ts` and `tests/vmd-gpu.ts` load/rasterize real GLSL/TSL paths and compare against independent numerical/pixel oracles across skinning, rigs, materials, serialized sources, poses and times. These tests have legitimate responsibilities. **The actual fraction of time spent compiling shaders versus drawing, reading pixels, loading assets and running JS has not been measured**, so do not assume a specific root cause beyond the observed suite durations and CPU-backed renderer.

## Expected outcome

The normal, free GitHub Actions CI becomes substantially faster by designing the test split **for CPU-backed SwiftShader**: run broad, deterministic combinatorial checks on the CPU wherever their assertions do not require an actual WebGL/TSL path; execute a small, deliberately selected but sufficient set of real shader/renderer cases on SwiftShader; and retain the meaningful mathematical, material, raster, lifecycle, fallback and edge-case guarantees.

A passing CPU-only model comparison is **not** a substitute for a GPU shader integration test, and SwiftShader alone does not establish behavior on hardware GPU drivers.

## Context and implementation direction

1. **Measure before changing coverage.** Use the existing `browser-summary.json` plus targeted instrumentation for major Solver and VMD phases (load/parse, shader compilation or first render, subsequent renders, vertex readback, raster comparison, waits and any screenshots). Collect repeatable evidence on the same Ubuntu runner. Avoid interpreting a whole test's duration as shader-compile time.
2. **Map coverage to execution mode.** Inventory the exact assertions / cross-products in `tests/browser/solver.spec.ts`, `tests/solver-gpu.ts`, `tests/browser/vmd.spec.ts`, `tests/vmd-gpu.ts`, and any other material hotspots. Distinguish:
   - **Node/CPU:** PMX/VMD decoding, IK/append/bone/morph math against independent scalar oracles, GLB/glTF serialization/reload and malformed/boundary cases (where available without a renderer).
   - **SwiftShader/WebGL:** actual shader compilation/execution, GPU vertex positions and normals, Toon/PBR and Outline raster correctness, runtime shader/plugin integration and representative asset/reload paths.
   - **Browser UI:** essential end-to-end controls, recovery, lifecycle and rendering synchronization.
3. **Refactor the remaining broad browser matrices.** Move provably renderer-independent assertions and cross-products into fast Node tests; for the real GPU paths, use a documented representative set covering each materially different shader branch, skinning family, rendering pass and required boundary/stress condition. Prefer sharing expensive setup and avoiding unnecessary renderer/shader reinitialization where tests remain independent and failure isolation is maintained.
4. **Preserve meaningful regression guarantees.** Do not silently omit the canonical BDEF/SDEF/QDEF shader paths, independent GPU position/normal probes, distinct Toon/PBR/Outline raster checks, IK/append semantics, morph/VMD/VPD behavior, large bone palettes, numerical edge cases, GLB/glTF/export compatibility, error recovery or prior regressions. A reduced permutation must be justified in a case-by-case coverage matrix showing which Node check or representative GPU case now covers it. Do not weaken tolerances, replace real render assertions with state-only checks, or simply skip tests.
5. **Keep the default workflow practical.** Prioritize improving work done per CPU-backed render, not just increasing timeout, `workers`, matrix parallelism or paid GPU runners. Keep GitHub Free/public-repo CI and deterministic production-build asset validation. Any later parallelization should be a separate, measured optimization.
6. **Document speed and coverage.** Record a full successful PR CI run's wall-clock browser time, per-suite hot spots and test outcomes, compared with successful #69/#70. Clearly distinguish implementation changes from pre-existing PR #53 improvements, and note any remaining bottlenecks or unavoidable SwiftShader limitations.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Start from (or integrate cleanly with) the Issue #52 / PR #53 browser-matrix cleanup, preserving its Uka integration and synthetic oracle coverage; do not revert earlier optimizations.
- [ ] Capture phase-level timing evidence for the heaviest browser suites, with a before/after comparison on comparable GitHub Actions CPU runners. Identify which costs are confirmed vs hypotheses.
- [ ] Provide an explicit coverage mapping for each removed/reduced GPU/browser permutation: assertions retained, Node or real-WebGL replacement, and reason it does not drop an independent shader/driver branch or stress regression.
- [ ] Move broad renderer-independent checks into Node tests where technically sound; retain real SwiftShader/GLTFLoader/plugin shader execution and pixel/vertex oracle comparisons for the representative paths and essential specialized cases.
- [ ] Keep all original numerical accuracy/raster thresholds and meaningful failure diagnostics; no silent skips, unsupported feature claims, or state-only substitutes for required rendering checks.
- [ ] Demonstrate a measurable, nontrivial reduction in browser CI duration against successful #69 (35.75 min) / #70 (34m21s) **without using extra runners or increased timeouts as the sole mechanism**. Include the test counts, pass/skip/failure counts, per-suite time deltas and all retained stress/format coverage. Do not assume a reduction target without measurement.
- [ ] The full PR CI passes: `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links` and `git diff --check`. Optional native-WebGPU skips remain explicitly marked.

## Optional validation

Run selected rendering cases on an actual hardware-GPU machine to complement (not replace) SwiftShader. Separately measure how much GitHub Actions job sharding would help after the test work itself has been optimized.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. This issue changes validation execution, not deployed runtime behavior. A successful full PR workflow is the mandatory pre-merge gate.

## Related work

- #52 / [PR #53](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/53): Uka example plus first round of synthetic browser matrix reduction, currently under review.
- [#69 successful PR CI](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/40697950655), [#70 successful PR CI](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/actions/runs/40706428394).
